dervis-irab:1-3.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَّخِذُوا عَدُوِّي وَعَدُوَّكُمْ أَوْلِياءَ تُلْقُونَ إِلَيْهِمْ بِالْمَوَدَّةِ):
يا is a vocative particle; أيّها is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, and the hāʾ is for alerting; الذين is a badal (substitute) of أيدي [Translator's note: so in the source, evidently a misprint for "أيّ"]; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause); لا is prohibitive; تتخذوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); عدوي is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) — it applies to one and more, because it is on the pattern of the maṣdar (verbal noun); عدوكم is conjoined to عدوي; and أولياء is the second mafʿūl bihi. The clause تلقون is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of تتخذوا; it may also be in the position of the accusative as an adjective of أولياء; or it may be explicative, with no grammatical position, [explaining] their taking them as allies. It has also been said that it is resumptive, brought to inform of that. تلقون is a verb and its fāʿil, and the mafʿūl bihi is omitted, its implied form being "the news of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ"; it has also been said that the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) and المودّة is the mafʿūl bihi, with no omission. إليهم is attached to (mutaʿalliq) تلقون.
(وَقَدْ كَفَرُوا بِما جاءَكُمْ مِنَ الْحَقِّ): the wāw is circumstantial; قد is a particle of realisation; كفروا is a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is a ḥāl from لا تتخذوا or from تلقون, the meaning being: do not love them while this is their state. بما is attached to كفروا; the clause جاءكم is the ṣila; and من الحق is a ḥāl.
(يُخْرِجُونَ الرَّسُولَ وَإِيَّاكُمْ أَنْ تُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ رَبِّكُمْ): the clause يخرجون is resumptive or explicative of their disbelief, so it has no grammatical position on either view; it may also be a ḥāl from the fāʿil of كفروا. الرسول is the object; إياكم is conjoined to الرسول; أن تؤمنوا is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. because of your believing in Allah; بالله is attached to تؤمنوا; and ربكم is a badal.
(إِنْ كُنْتُمْ خَرَجْتُمْ جِهاداً فِي سَبِيلِي وَابْتِغاءَ مَرْضاتِي): إن is conditional; كنتم is a defective past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the tāʾ is its noun; the clause خرجتم is the predicate of كنتم; جهادا is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, i.e. for the sake of jihad — and the accusative may also be as a ḥāl, i.e. in the state of your being strivers. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by His saying لا تتخذوا.
(تُسِرُّونَ إِلَيْهِمْ بِالْمَوَدَّةِ وَأَنَا أَعْلَمُ بِما أَخْفَيْتُمْ وَما أَعْلَنْتُمْ): the clause تسرون is either resumptive or subordinate to تلقون إليهم as a badal of part for whole, because conveying love is more general than [doing so] secretly and openly. تسرون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil; the mafʿūl bihi is omitted; بالمودّة is attached to تسرون, or the bāʾ is redundant in the object, after the pattern of what preceded in تلقون إليهم بالمودّة. The wāw is circumstantial; أنا is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and أعلم the khabar (predicate), as an elative (ism tafḍīl); بما is attached to أعلم; the clause أخفيتم is the ṣila of ما. أعلم may also be an imperfect verb. وما أعلنتم is conjoined to بما أخفيتم.
(وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْهُ مِنْكُمْ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ سَواءَ السَّبِيلِ): the wāw is conjunctive or resumptive; من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; يفعله is the protasis, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir), its implied form being "هو", and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿ links the apodosis because it is joined with قد; ضلّ is a verb whose fāʿil is هو, and سواء السبيل is its object. It has also been said that ضلّ is intransitive, so سواء السبيل is accusative as an adverb of place.
(إِنْ يَثْقَفُوكُمْ يَكُونُوا لَكُمْ أَعْداءً): إن is conditional; يثقفوكم is the protasis, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil and the kāf the mafʿūl bihi; يكونوا is the apodosis, the sign of its jussive also being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its noun and أعداء its predicate; and لكم is a ḥāl. In al-Miṣbāḥ:
«ثقفت الشيء ثقفا, of the pattern of تعب: I took it; ثقفت الرجل في الحرب: I caught up with him; ثقفته: I got the better of him; ثقفت الحديث: I understood it quickly; the active participle is ثقيف.»
(وَيَبْسُطُوا إِلَيْكُمْ أَيْدِيَهُمْ وَأَلْسِنَتَهُمْ بِالسُّوءِ): conjoined to يكونوا; إليكم is attached to يبسطوا; أيديهم is the mafʿūl bihi; ألسنتهم is conjoined to أيديهم; and بالسوء is a ḥāl.
(وَوَدُّوا لَوْ تَكْفُرُونَ): also conjoined, to the clause of condition and consequence; so He the Exalted has given two pieces of information: what the conditional clause contains, and their wishing that the believers disbelieve. The secret of the shift from the imperfect to the past will come. لو is maṣdar-forming; تكفرون is an imperfect verb, nominative; and لو with what lies in its scope is a maṣdar in the position of the accusative as the object of ودّوا.
(لَنْ تَنْفَعَكُمْ أَرْحامُكُمْ وَلا أَوْلادُكُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَكُمْ): a resumptive statement brought to make known that their kin and children will not benefit them. لن is a particle of negation, accusative and futurity; تنفعكم is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by لن; the kāf is a fronted mafʿūl bihi and أرحامكم a postponed fāʿil; ولا أولادكم is conjoined to أرحامكم. يوم القيامة is an adverb attached to what precedes it, i.e. "they will not benefit you on the Day of Resurrection", with a pause on it; or attached to what follows it, i.e. "He will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection". يفصل is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is هو, i.e. Allah the Exalted; and يُفصَل has been read in the passive. بينكم is an adverb attached to يفصل in any case.
(وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ): الله is a mubtadaʾ; بما is attached to بصير; the clause تعملون is the ṣila; and بصير is the khabar of الله.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «وودّوا لو تكفرون» He shifted from the imperfect, which suits what precedes it, to the past, although the context requires it to be a future imperfect, by regarding it as having already happened; i.e. their wishing for your disbelief is what matters to them, and nothing equals it in weight. That is, they want to inflict on you all the harms of this world and of religion, and your reverting to disbelief is the foremost of the harms to you, because they know that religion is dearer to you than your lives. This is of the wonderful [modes of] expression.

* Benefits:
It is now time to convey to you a full summary of the story because of which the sura was revealed, for the enjoyment and benefit in it. The Imams have related — the wording being Muslim's — from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me, al-Zubayr and al-Miqdād, and said: "Go to Rawḍat Khākh" — [read] as a triptote and as a diptote — a place twelve miles from Medina, "for there is a woman travelling in a litter there who has a letter; take it from her." So we set off, our horses racing (nuhādī), i.e. we made them go fast, and there we came upon a woman. We said, "Bring out the letter." She said, "I have no letter." We said, "You will bring out the letter, or you will cast off your clothes." So she brought it out from her braids, and we brought it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and in it was: From Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿa to some people among the idolaters of Mecca, informing them of something of the affair of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Ḥāṭib, what is this?" He said: "Do not hasten against me, O Messenger of Allah. I was a man attached to Quraysh" — Sufyān said: he was their ally and not one of them — "and those emigrants who are with you have kinsmen by whom they protect their families. Since I lacked that kinship among them, I wanted to do them a favour by which they would protect my relatives. I did not do it out of disbelief, nor apostasy from my religion, nor contentment with disbelief after Islam. And I knew that Allah would send down His might upon them, that my letter would not avail them anything, and that Allah would grant you victory over them." The Prophet ﷺ said: "He has spoken the truth." ʿUmar said: "Let me, O Messenger of Allah, strike the neck of this hypocrite." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "He witnessed Badr; and what do you know — perhaps Allah looked upon the people of Badr and said: Do what you will, for I have forgiven you." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: «يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا عدوي وعدوكم أولياء» (the verse). It has been said that the woman's name was Sāra, and she was a freedwoman of Abū ʿAmr ibn Ṣayfī ibn Hāshim.

The text of the letter:
As for the text of Ḥāṭib's letter, it is: «To proceed: the Messenger of Allah has set out towards you with an army like the night, moving like a torrent. I swear by Allah, if he marched against you alone, Allah would give him victory over you and fulfil His promise to him concerning you, for Allah is his Protector and Helper.»
Al-Qushayrī and al-Thaʿlabī mentioned that Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿa was a man from the people of Yemen, and in Mecca he was an ally of the Banū Asad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, the clan of al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām; it has also been said he was an ally of al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām. Sāra came from Mecca to Medina while the Messenger of Allah was preparing for the conquest of Mecca. The Messenger of Allah said to her: "Have you come as an emigrant, O Sāra?" She said: "No." He said: "Have you come as a Muslim?" She said: "No." He said: "Then what brought you?"
She said: "You were the family, the patrons, the root and the clan; some of the patrons have gone" — meaning they were killed on the day of Badr — "and I have fallen into severe need, so I have come to you that you may give to me and clothe me." He, upon him be blessing and peace, said: "And where are you with respect to the young men of Mecca?" — she was a singer. She said: "Nothing has been requested of me since the battle of Badr." So the Messenger of Allah urged the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib to give to her, and they clothed her, gave her a mount and gave to her. She set out for Mecca, and Ḥāṭib came to her and said: "I will give you ten dinars and a cloak on condition that you deliver this letter to the people of Mecca." And he wrote in the letter: "The Messenger of Allah intends [to attack] you, so take your precautions" — to the end of the story.

dervis-irab:4-7.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أُسْوَةٌ): with ḍamma and with kasra on the hamza, and it has been read with both; i.e. the model, and that by which one consoles oneself. The plural is أسى, also with ḍamma and kasra on the hamza.
(بَراءٌ): plural of بريء, like ظريف and ظرفاء; it also has the plural براء with kasra on the bāʾ, like ظريف and ظراف [Translator's note: the source prints "ظرف"]; and براء with ḍamma on the bāʾ, like تؤام and ظؤار; and أبراء and أبرياء. البريء is the pure, the free [of something], and the opposite of the guilty and the accused.

* I'rab:
(قَدْ كانَتْ لَكُمْ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ فِي إِبْراهِيمَ وَالَّذِينَ مَعَهُ): a resumptive statement brought to strike the example worthy of imitation in the prohibition of befriending the disbelievers and inclining towards enemies, and [to show] that breasts folded upon rancour must remain in their enmity until the existing cause disappears; when it disappears, enmity turns to affection and hatred to love. قد is a particle of realisation; كانت is a defective past verb; لكم is its fronted predicate and أسوة its postponed noun; and حسنة is a naʿt (adjective) of أسوة. As for في إبراهيم:
you may attach it to an omitted [word] as a second adjective of أسوة, or as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it, since it has been qualified. The wording of Abū al-Baqāʾ: «There are several views on it: first, it is another adjective of أسوة; second, it is attached to حسنة as an adverbial is attached to its governor; third, that it be a ḥāl from the pronoun in حسنة; fourth, that it be the predicate of كان, and لكم is an explanation. It may not be attached to أسوة, because it has been qualified.» A number of parsers rejected the last point of Abū al-Baqāʾ, because with adverbials [and prepositional phrases] what is overlooked is not overlooked with others. الذين is conjoined to إبراهيم; and معه is an adverb of place attached to an omitted [word], which is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين.
(إِذْ قالُوا لِقَوْمِهِمْ إِنَّا بُرَآؤُا مِنْكُمْ وَمِمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ): إذ is an adverb of past time, i.e. "when they said", and it is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) of إبراهيم والذين معه; this is the best of the strained parsings mentioned by Abū al-Baqāʾ and others. The clause قالوا is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being annexed to it; لقومهم is attached to (mutaʿalliq) قالوا; إنّ and its noun, and برآء is its predicate, the clause being the object of their saying (maqūl al-qawl); منكم is attached to برآء; مما is conjoined to منكم; the clause تعبدون is the ṣila; and من دون الله is a ḥāl.
(كَفَرْنا بِكُمْ وَبَدا بَيْنَنا وَبَيْنَكُمُ الْعَداوَةُ وَالْبَغْضاءُ أَبَداً حَتَّى تُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَحْدَهُ): the clause explains the disowning of them and of what they worship; you may also make it a ḥāl, i.e. we have disowned you, being disbelievers in you. كفرنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); بكم is attached to كفرنا; بدا is a past verb; بيننا is an adverb attached to بدا; بينكم is an adverb conjoined to بيننا; العداوة is the fāʿil; البغضاء is conjoined to العداوة; أبدا is an adverb also attached to بدا; حتى is a particle of limit and genitive; تؤمنوا is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتى; بالله is attached to تؤمنوا; and وحده is a ḥāl.
(إِلَّا قَوْلَ إِبْراهِيمَ لِأَبِيهِ لَأَسْتَغْفِرَنَّ لَكَ وَما أَمْلِكُ لَكَ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ): إلا is a particle of exception; قول إبراهيم is excepted from أسوة حسنة, because the saying is part of the model; so it is a connected exception, as if it were said: you have in him a good model in all his states of word and deed, except his saying such-and-such. It has also been said that it is a disconnected exception, the meaning being: but Ibrāhīm's saying to his father "I will surely ask forgiveness for you" — do not imitate him in it. The wording of Abū Ḥayyān: It appears that it is part of the completion of Ibrāhīm's saying, connected with what precedes the exception, and it is among the things in which he is to be imitated; the exception separates them out of concern for the exception and because of its closeness to what is excepted from. لأبيه is attached to قول. لأستغفرنّ: the lām prepares for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa); أستغفرن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because of its connection with the heavy nūn of emphasis; the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "أنا"; the clause is the object of the saying; and لك is attached to أستغفرنّ. The wāw is circumstantial or conjunctive, since the clause is part of the completion of Ibrāhīm's saying; so it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of أستغفرنّ, i.e. "I will ask forgiveness for you, and nothing is within my power but asking forgiveness"; so it is built on what precedes it and arranged after it by way of being a ḥāl; and conjunction is also permissible. ما is negating; أملك is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "أنا"; لك is attached to أملك; من الله is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of شيء; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; and شيء is genitive in form and accusative in position as the object of أملك.
(رَبَّنا عَلَيْكَ تَوَكَّلْنا وَإِلَيْكَ أَنَبْنا وَإِلَيْكَ الْمَصِيرُ): the completion of what was said by al-Khalīl Ibrāhīm and those with him; so it belongs to what is excepted from, and he is to be imitated in it. So in meaning it comes before the exception, and the exception clause is parenthetical in the midst of what is excepted from. The wording of al-Kashshāf: «If you say: with what is His saying ربنا عليك توكلنا connected? I say: with what precedes the exception, and it is part of the good model. It may also mean: "Say: Our Lord", as a command from Allah the Exalted to the believers to say it, and a teaching from Him to them, completing what He enjoined on them of cutting the ties between them and the disbelievers, and of following the example of Ibrāhīm and his people in disowning them; and drawing attention to turning to Allah and seeking refuge in Him from the trial of the people of disbelief, and seeking forgiveness for what they had neglected.» I.e. it is then the object of an omitted saying. ربنا is the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf; عليك is attached to توكلنا; إليك is attached to أنبنا; the wāw is conjunctive; إليك is a fronted khabar (predicate) and المصير a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).
(رَبَّنا لا تَجْعَلْنا فِتْنَةً لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَاغْفِرْ لَنا رَبَّنا إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ): ربنا is also the one addressed, a muḍāf; لا is prohibitive, intended as supplication; تجعلنا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا; نا is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and فتنة the second mafʿūl bihi. It is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of the agent, i.e. do not make us a cause of trial to them by their gaining victory over us, so that their minds are shaken and they are tempted, and their souls entice them [to think] that they are in the right; or in the sense of the patient, as al-Bayḍāwī set out, i.e. do not make us
tried by them by giving them power over us, so that they try us with a punishment we have no strength to bear. للذين is attached to فتنة on both views; the clause كفروا is the ṣila of the relative noun; ربنا is the one addressed, a muḍāf, repeated for emphasis; إنّ and its noun; أنت is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ; العزيز is the khabar of إنّ, or the khabar of أنت, the clause then being the khabar of إنّ; and الحكيم is a second khabar in either case.
(لَقَدْ كانَ لَكُمْ فِيهِمْ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ لِمَنْ كانَ يَرْجُوا اللَّهَ وَالْيَوْمَ الْآخِرَ): the clause follows the clause قد كانت لكم أسوة as an emphasis of it, brought for intensity in urging the ruling. The lām prepares for an implied oath; قد is a particle of realisation; كان is a defective past verb; لكم is its fronted predicate; فيهم is a ḥāl; أسوة is the postponed noun of كان and حسنة an adjective of أسوة; لمن is a badal of part for whole of لكم, with repetition of the preposition — it has also been said to be a badal of inclusion; the clause كان is the ṣila of من; the noun of كان is latent, its implied form being "هو"; the clause يرجو الله is the predicate of كان; and اليوم الآخر is conjoined to الله.
(وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ): the wāw is resumptive; من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; يتول is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; the fāʿ links the apodosis, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being "then the evil consequence of his turning away is upon himself"; and إنّ with its noun and its two predicates is the reason for the apodosis.
(عَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَجْعَلَ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَ الَّذِينَ عادَيْتُمْ مِنْهُمْ مَوَدَّةً): عسى is one of the verbs of hope; الله is its noun; أن يجعل is in the place of the predicate; بينكم is an adverb in the place of the second object of يجعل; بين الذين عاديتهم [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has عاديتم] is conjoined to the adverb; مودّة is the first object of يجعل; and منهم is a ḥāl from الذين عاديتم.
(وَاللَّهُ قَدِيرٌ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): a mubtadaʾ and a khabar, with their like conjoined to them.

dervis-irab:8-9.t:
* I'rab:
(لا يَنْهاكُمُ اللَّهُ عَنِ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يُقاتِلُوكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ): a resumptive statement brought to explain the permission to maintain ties with those who did not fight the believers and did not expel them from their homes. لا is negating; ينهاكم الله is an imperfect verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and a postponed fāʿil (agent); عن الذين is attached to (mutaʿalliq) ينهاكم; the clause لم يقاتلوكم is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; and في الدين is attached to يقاتلوكم, i.e. on account of it.
(وَلَمْ يُخْرِجُوكُمْ مِنْ دِيارِكُمْ أَنْ تَبَرُّوهُمْ وَتُقْسِطُوا إِلَيْهِمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُقْسِطِينَ): ولم يخرجوكم is conjoined to لم يقاتلوكم; من دياركم is attached to يخرجوكم; أن تبرّوهم is in the position of the genitive as a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) of الذين; وتقسطوا إليهم is conjoined to تبروهم; and إنّ with its noun, the clause يحبّ المقسطين being its predicate. Beautiful is al-Zamakhsharī's saying in this connection: «And it suffices you that Allah's enjoining the believers to deal justly with those who associate partners with Him and to avoid wronging them speaks eloquently of the state of a Muslim who dares to wrong his Muslim brother.»
(إِنَّما يَنْهاكُمُ اللَّهُ عَنِ الَّذِينَ قاتَلُوكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ): إنما is [إنّ] restrained [from governing] by the restraining [ما] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); ينهاكم الله is an imperfect verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi and a postponed fāʿil; عن الذين is attached to ينهاكم; the clause قاتلوكم is the ṣila of الذين; and في الدين is attached to قاتلوكم.
(وَأَخْرَجُوكُمْ مِنْ دِيارِكُمْ وَظاهَرُوا عَلى إِخْراجِكُمْ أَنْ تَوَلَّوْهُمْ): أخرجوكم is conjoined to قاتلوكم; من دياركم is attached to أخرجوكم; ظاهروا is also conjoined; على إخراجكم is attached to ظاهروا, i.e. they helped in expelling you; and أن with what lies in its scope is a badal of inclusion of الذين. Its counterpart has preceded.
(وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّهُمْ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; من is a jussive conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); يتولهم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʿ is linking; the clause أولئك هم الظالمون is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of من.

dervis-irab:10-13.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فَامْتَحِنُوهُنَّ): then test them and try them. That is why the sura was named al-Mumtaḥina, with kasra on the ḥāʾ, i.e. the one that tests — meaning the woman or the group that tests, since in it the group of believers is commanded to test. If the ḥāʾ is given fatḥa, the meaning is "the sura of the emigrant woman" concerning whom the verse of testing was revealed; her story will come in the section on benefits.
(بِعِصَمِ الْكَوافِرِ): العصم is the plural of عصمة, which here is the marriage contract; everything by which a thing is held fast is عصام and عصمة. The properties of [roots with] ʿayn and ṣād as first and second radicals have passed. الكوافر is the plural of كافرة, like ضوارب from ضاربة. The wording of Abū Ḥayyān: «Al-Karkhī said: الكوافر includes men and women. Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī said to him: The grammarians hold this only for women, as the plural of كافرة. He said: Is it not said طائفة كافرة (a disbelieving faction) and فرقة كافرة (a disbelieving sect)? Abū ʿAlī said: I was dumbfounded, and I said: This is a confirmation.» This al-Karkhī was a Muʿtazilite jurist, and Abū ʿAlī was also a Muʿtazilite, so this derivation pleased him; but it amounts to nothing, because كافرة is not said in describing men except as following its qualified noun, or with that noun omitted but intended; otherwise, فاعلة is not pluralised as فواعل except when it is for the feminine.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذا جاءَكُمُ الْمُؤْمِناتُ مُهاجِراتٍ فَامْتَحِنُوهُنَّ): إذا is an adverb of future time, putting its condition in the genitive and made accusative by its apodosis; the clause جاءكم is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being annexed to it; المؤمنات is a postponed fāʿil (agent); مهاجرات is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the fāʿ is linking; and the clause امتحنوهنّ has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; it is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
(اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِإِيمانِهِنَّ فَإِنْ عَلِمْتُمُوهُنَّ مُؤْمِناتٍ فَلا تَرْجِعُوهُنَّ إِلَى الْكُفَّارِ): الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and أعلم the khabar (predicate); بإيمانهنّ is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أعلم, because it is an elative (afʿal tafḍīl). The fāʿ is conjunctive; إن is conditional; علمتموهنّ is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) — a verb, its fāʿil and its first mafʿūl bihi — and مؤمنات is the second mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) because it is a request clause; لا is prohibitive; ترجعوهنّ is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; and إلى الكفّار is attached to ترجعوهنّ.
(لا هُنَّ حِلٌّ لَهُمْ وَلا هُمْ يَحِلُّونَ لَهُنَّ): the clause has no grammatical position because it gives the reason for His saying فلا ترجعوهنّ. لا is negating; هنّ is a mubtadaʾ and حلّ the khabar; لهم is attached to حلّ; and ولا هم يحلّون لهنّ is conjoined to the preceding clause, parallel to it.
(وَآتُوهُمْ ما أَنْفَقُوا): the wāw is conjunctive; آتوهم is a past verb [Translator's note: so in the source; it is an imperative], its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, the pronoun referring to the disbelievers, i.e. give their disbelieving husbands what they spent on them. ما is the second mafʿūl bihi, and the clause أنفقوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما, i.e. what they spent on them of dowries.
(وَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْ تَنْكِحُوهُنَّ إِذا آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ): the wāw is conjunctive; لا is the lā of generic negation; جناح is its noun, indeclinable on the fatḥa; عليكم is the predicate of لا; أن is a maṣdar-forming and accusative particle; تنكحوهنّ is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن, and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. "in your marrying them", the preposition and its noun being attached to جناح. إذا is an adverb containing the meaning of condition; the clause آتيتموهنّ is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being annexed to it; and أجورهنّ is the second object of آتيتموهنّ.
(وَلا تُمْسِكُوا بِعِصَمِ الْكَوافِرِ): the wāw is conjunctive; لا is prohibitive; تمسكوا is an imperfect verb, jussive by لا, and the wāw is the fāʿil; and بعصم الكوافر is attached to تمسكوا.
(وَسْئَلُوا ما أَنْفَقْتُمْ وَلْيَسْئَلُوا ما أَنْفَقُوا): the wāw is conjunctive; اسألوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil and ما is the mafʿūl bihi; the clause أنفقتم has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of ما. وليسألوا: the wāw is conjunctive, the lām is the lām of command, يسألوا is an imperfect verb, jussive by the lām of command, ما is the mafʿūl bihi, and the clause أنفقوا is the ṣila.
(ذلِكُمْ حُكْمُ اللَّهِ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ): ذلكم is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the ruling contained in the verses, and حكم الله is the khabar; the clause يحكم is resumptive or a ḥāl from حكم الله; بينكم is an adverb attached to يحكم; الله is a mubtadaʾ, عليم a first khabar and حكيم a second khabar.
(وَإِنْ فاتَكُمْ شَيْءٌ مِنْ أَزْواجِكُمْ إِلَى الْكُفَّارِ فَعاقَبْتُمْ فَآتُوا الَّذِينَ ذَهَبَتْ أَزْواجُهُمْ مِثْلَ ما أَنْفَقُوا): the wāw is conjunctive, so that the rulings follow in sequence. إن is conditional; فاتكم is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis; شيء is the fāʿil of فاتكم. In من أزواجكم there are two views. The first: it may be attached to فاتكم, i.e. on the part of your wives, and by "something" is meant the dowry the husband paid, since it has come down that when a Muslim man's wife fled to the disbelievers, Allah commanded the believers to give him what he had paid. The second view: it is attached to an omitted [word] as an adjective of شيء; then شيء may mean what preceded of dowries, but on this view a muḍāf must be omitted, i.e. "of the dowries of your wives", so that the qualified noun and its adjective correspond; or شيء may mean the women, i.e. a kind and category of them. إلى الكفار is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. going or preceding. فعاقبتم: the fāʿ is conjunctive and عاقبتم is a verb and its fāʿil, i.e. then you raided, took booty and struck them in fighting. فآتوا: the fāʿ is linking; آتوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis; الذين is the mafʿūl bihi; the clause ذهبت أزواجهم is the ṣila; مثل is the second mafʿūl bihi; ما is a relative noun to which مثل is annexed; and the clause أنفقوا is the ṣila.
(وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي أَنْتُمْ بِهِ مُؤْمِنُونَ): اتقوا الله is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; الذي is a naʿt (adjective); أنتم is a mubtadaʾ; به is attached to مؤمنون; مؤمنون is the khabar of أنتم; and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of الذي.
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ إِذا جاءَكَ الْمُؤْمِناتُ يُبايِعْنَكَ عَلى أَنْ لا يُشْرِكْنَ بِاللَّهِ شَيْئاً): إذا is a future adverb containing the meaning of condition; the clause جاءك is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being annexed to it; the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi and المؤمنات the fāʿil; يبايعنك is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the sukūn because of its connection with the nūn of the feminine plural; the nūn is the fāʿil and the kāf the mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is circumstantial, i.e. in the state of their seeking to pledge allegiance. على is a preposition, and أن with what lies in its scope is in the position of the genitive by على, the preposition and its noun being attached to يبايعنك; and شيئا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. anything of associating partners.
(وَلا يَسْرِقْنَ وَلا يَزْنِينَ وَلا يَقْتُلْنَ أَوْلادَهُنَّ وَلا يَأْتِينَ بِبُهْتانٍ يَفْتَرِينَهُ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِنَّ وَأَرْجُلِهِنَّ وَلا يَعْصِينَكَ فِي مَعْرُوفٍ فَبايِعْهُنَّ): speech conjoined to أن لا يشركن. The meaning of يقتلن أولادهنّ is as was the case in the time of the Jāhiliyya, of burying daughters alive. ببهتان is attached to يأتين; the clause يفترينه is circumstantial; بين أيديهنّ وأرجلهنّ: the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl from the accusative pronoun in يفترينه, i.e. they bring a foundling child and attribute it to the husband. Beautiful is its being described with the attribute of a real child, for when a mother gives birth to a child it falls between her hands and her feet. فبايعهنّ: the fāʿ links the answer of إذا, and the clause بايعهنّ has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
(وَاسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُنَّ اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): the wāw is conjunctive; استغفر is an imperative verb; لهنّ is attached to استغفر; الله is the mafʿūl bihi; and the clause إن الله غفور رحيم is the reason for the command to seek forgiveness.
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَوَلَّوْا قَوْماً غَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ): a resumptive statement brought to close the sura with the like of what it opened with: the prohibition of taking the disbelievers as allies. لا is prohibitive; تتولوا is an imperfect verb, jussive by لا, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; قوما is the mafʿūl bihi; and the clause غضب الله عليهم is an adjective of قوما.
(قَدْ يَئِسُوا مِنَ الْآخِرَةِ كَما يَئِسَ الْكُفَّارُ مِنْ أَصْحابِ الْقُبُورِ): the clause is a second adjective of قوما, or a ḥāl after it has been qualified. قد is a particle of realisation; يئسوا is a verb and its fāʿil; من الآخرة is attached to يئسوا; كما is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); يئس الكفار is a verb and its fāʿil, the clause having no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the particle-relative. In من أصحاب القبور there are two views. One: من is for the beginning of the extent, like the first [من], and the meaning is that they do not at all believe with certainty in the resurrection of the dead, so their despair of the Hereafter is like their despair of their dead, because they believe they will not be raised. The second: من is for explaining the genus, meaning that the disbelievers are the people of the graves; so the preposition and its noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl, and what the second يئس is attached to is omitted, the meaning being: these have despaired of the Hereafter just as the disbelievers, being among the people of the graves, have despaired of the good of the Hereafter.

* Rhetoric:
In the saying of Allah the Exalted: «يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتولوا قوما غضب الله عليهم قد يئسوا من الآخرة كما يئس الكفّار من أصحاب القبور» there is the device of istiṭrād (digression), a lofty device among the devices of bayān. Al-Ḥātimī mentioned that he took this name from the poet al-Buḥturī, and Ibn al-Muʿtazz called it "going out from one meaning to another". Of it in the Glorious Qur'an is «ألا بعدا لمدين كما بعدت ثمود», for here He digressed. In the verse we are dealing with, He censured the Jews and digressed from censuring them to censuring the idolaters, with a fine kind of relation. Istiṭrād linguistically is the maṣdar of استطرد الفارس من قرنه في الحرب (the horseman feigned flight from his opponent in war), that is, he flees from before him, making him imagine defeat, then wheels round on him while he is off guard. Technically, it is that you are on one of the themes of poetry, making it seem that you are continuing in it, then you go out from it to another because of a relation between them; the name of the one digressed to must be stated explicitly, on condition that he has not been mentioned before; then you return to the first, or it is the end of the speech. It has been said that the first instance of this kind that has come down and become proverbial is the saying of al-Samawʾal:
وإنّا لقوم لا نرى القتل سبة ... إذا ما رأته عامر وسلول
(We are a people who do not consider being killed a disgrace, whereas ʿĀmir and Salūl consider it so.)
See how he went out, while engaged in boasting, into satire, and how finely he returned to what he had been on of boasting by his saying:
يقرب حب الموت آجالنا لنا ... وتكرهه آجالهم فتطول
(Love of death brings our appointed terms near to us, while their terms hate it and so grow long.)
And of it is the saying of Ḥassān ibn Thābit:
إن كنت كاذبة الذي حدّثتني ... فنجوت منجى الحارث بن هشام
ترك الأحبة أن يقاتل دونهم ... ونجا برأس طمرة ولجام
(If you have lied in what you told me, then may you escape as al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām escaped: he left his loved ones rather than fight for them, and escaped on the head of a swift mare with a bridle.)
See how he went out from love poetry to satirising al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām, the brother of Abū Jahl, who embraced Islam on the day of the Conquest, became a good Muslim, and died on the day of al-Yarmūk in Syria. Also of it is the saying of al-Buḥturī, from an ode describing a horse:
كالهيكل المبني إلا أنه ... في الحسن جاء كصورة في هيكل
ملك العيون فإن بدا أعطيته ... نظر المحب إلى الحبيب المقبل
ما إن يعاف قذى ولو أوردته ... يوما خلائق حمدويه الأحول
(Like a built temple, except that in beauty it came like an image in a temple; it masters the eyes, and when it appears you give it the look of a lover at the approaching beloved; it does not shun dirty water, even if one day you led it to water at the character of squint-eyed Ḥamdawayh.)
And like it is the saying of someone describing wine that was cooked until it became clear and pure:
لم يبق منها وقود الطابخين لها ... إلا كما أبقت الأنواء من داري
(The fire of those who cooked it left of it only as much as the rain-storms have left of my house.)
How sweet is his digression from describing the wine to describing his house as ruined!
Among the rarities of this chapter is digression from satire to satire, as in the saying of Jarīr satirising al-Farazdaq:
لها برص بأسفل أسكيتها ... كعنفقة الفرزدق حين شابا
(She has leprous patches on the lower sides of her private parts, like al-Farazdaq's chin-tuft when it turned grey.)

* Benefits:
This sura contains historical and legislative benefits; we cite those of them related to the subject of our book, and refer the reader to the books of jurisprudence and the lengthy commentaries:
1- History relates that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had finished receiving the pledge of the men on the day of the Conquest of Mecca, he began receiving the pledge of the women while he was on al-Ṣafā, with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb below him taking their pledge at his command and conveying to them from him. Hind bint ʿUtba, the wife of Abū Sufyān, was veiled and disguised among the women, fearing that the Messenger of Allah would recognise her because of what she had done to Ḥamza on the day of Uḥud. She said: "By Allah, you are taking from us an undertaking that I did not see you take from the men" — that day he had taken the pledge of the men on Islam and jihad only. The Messenger of Allah said: "And that they will not steal." She said: "Abū Sufyān is stingy, and I have taken small amounts of his wealth; I do not know whether they are lawful for me or not." Abū Sufyān said: "Whatever you took in what is past and what remains is lawful for you." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed and recognised her, and said to her: "And you are indeed Hind bint ʿUtba?" She said: "Yes, so pardon what is past, O Prophet of Allah, may Allah pardon you." He said: "And that they will not commit fornication." She said: "Does a free woman commit fornication?"
In one narration: "No woman among them has ever committed fornication." He, upon him be blessing and peace, said: "And that they will not kill their children." She said: "We raised them when small and you killed them when grown; you and they know best" — her son Ḥanẓala ibn Abī Sufyān had been killed on the day of Badr. ʿUmar laughed until he fell on his back, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled. He said: "And that they will not bring a slander." She said: "By Allah, slander is an ugly thing, and you command us only to right guidance and noble character." He said: "And that they will not disobey you in what is right." She said: "By Allah, we have not sat in this sitting of ours with any thought in ourselves of disobeying you in anything."
2- Various narrations have been mentioned about the manner of burying daughters alive; we consider the closest of them to reason what has been narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: «In the Jāhiliyya, when a woman's delivery drew near, she would dig a pit and go into labour at the edge of the pit; if she gave birth to a girl she threw her into the pit and put the earth back over her, and if she gave birth to a boy she kept him. And in the Jāhiliyya, when a daughter was born to a man and he wanted to let her live, he would clothe her in a garment of wool or hair, and she would herd camels and sheep for him in the desert; and if he wanted to kill her, he would leave her until, when she was "sudāsiyya", i.e. six years old, he would say to her mother: Perfume her and adorn her, so that I may take her to her in-laws. He would have dug a well for her in the desert, and he would take her to the well and say to her: Look into it; then he would push her from behind and heap the earth upon her.
[Translator's note: the closing quotation mark of Ibn ʿAbbās's report is missing in the source.]
